data.summary: A gated verb named [REDACTED:host] was written to ask.requested as [REDACTED:host] (host-name redaction takes a word ending .local for a machine name), so the stored verb never equals the canon verb and every approval of it is refused as 'an approval for [REDACTED:host]'. The verb field is declared verbatim in LOG_VERBATIM_FIELDS yet is still redacted. Repro: ddflow export enable changelog --local with --agent bot under a site named [REDACTED:host], then read asks_of(state)[id]['verb']. Worked around by naming the site export.machine.
data.title: An approval verb ending in .local is stored as [REDACTED:host]

data.claim: On the base commit an agent identity (--agent bot) can run `export enable X --local` and `export --update --force` and the relayed `--yes --reason` verbs with no approval, because the only guard was a parity exemption (MCP lacks the flags), not a refusal.
data.falsifier: The base commit's test_enable_local_writes_the_local_layer_only (agent bot, --local) failing, or a refusal naming an approval.
data.mechanism: The flags are CLI-only; no marker call (is_agent) sits on those paths, so sites.py listed them as NOT_YET_ROUTED rather than as gated sites.
data.probe: uv run pytest tests/test_export_select.py::test_enable_local_writes_the_local_layer_only (on git archive of the base commit)
data.probe_output: Passed on base (assert run_cli(proj,'export','enable','bugs','--local',agent='bot')[0]==0); on this branch the same call exits 3 and files an export.machine request.
data.question: Are export --force/--local and relayed-consent verbs reachable by an agent identity without a person's approval on main?

evidence.note: research R9558a6111c CONFIRMED: base let an agent run --local/--force and relayed verbs unapproved (base test passed with agent bot)
